summary: Huawen Bai worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Peking University (~1951–1955), where he later served as Professor (~1979–2000).

Hubert Decleer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Hotel- en Toerismeschool Spermalie, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at the School for International Training, Middlebury College, and the University of Vienna.

Hubert Durt specialized in Buddhist studies, having studied under Étienne Lamotte (~1958–1965). He served as editor-in-chief and Professor at EFEO, director of the Hōbōgirin Institute (~1980–2001), and Professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2010).

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and served as Associate Professor at Ohio State University (~2004–2008).
Hugh Gray was active in Indology and other fields. He studied at Battersea Grammar School and held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 1983.
Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who studied at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, the University of Klagenfurt, and the University of Turin.
Hugh Richardson was a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Keble College (~1924–1928) and worked for the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1947).

Hugo David specializes in Indology and philosophy. After earning a PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études (–2012) and studying with several traditional teachers, he held a fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and joined EFEO as a permanent member in 2015.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Jing-shen Tao, as well as under traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi (attested 2003).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).

Huimin specializes in Buddhist studies and studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He held posts at TNUA, the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and served as President of Dharma Drum Buddhist College (~2007–2014).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under Kuo-wei Liu, having also studied under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, while also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held an attested lecturer post at Dongguk University in 1996.

Humberto Maturana worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Liceo Manuel de Salas, University College London (~1954–1956), and Harvard University (~1956–1958), later holding a post at the University of Chile (~1960).
Hung-Yi Yang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Mark Allon.

Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago, held a professorship at MIT (~1958–1973), and was Thomas J. Watson Professor Emeritus at Syracuse University.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under the instruction of Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Choi also held a post as Visiting Researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), and Harvard University (~1989–1992), and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn (~1990–2004).
